description: A random voltage and a random gate, both drawn fresh each time the input jack crosses 1V

params.text: Sets the limit the sampled voltage is clamped to, 0.25V to 10V; in bipolar mode that limit applies either side of zero, in unipolar mode from zero upwards
Switches the sampled voltage between swinging either side of zero and running from zero upwards; past the halfway point of its travel it is bipolar
Multiplies the raw random draw before it is clamped, 1 to 10 in whole steps; above 1 most draws land on the clamp, so the sampled voltage arrives near the ends of its range
Multiplies the GATE LENGTH setting before each gate is decided: position 1 by 0.25, position 2 by 0.125, position 3 by 0.625, so the middle position makes a gate least likely
Biases the chance that each new sample gives a 10V gate rather than 0V, scaled by the three-position switch; it sets no duration, despite the panel printing GATE LENGTH
Nothing in the module reads this control. The value it feeds is computed into a gate-speed figure that is then discarded, so the incoming trigger is never divided.
Added to the sampled voltage after the clamp, -5V to 5V, so it can push the S&H output past the Range setting

inputs.text: A level of 1V or more takes a new random sample and a new gate; the level must fall back below 1V before another can be taken, and the module produces nothing at all until one arrives

outputs.text: 10V or 0V, drawn at random each time the input triggers and held until the next trigger
The random voltage drawn at the last trigger, clamped to the Range setting and then shifted by the OFFSET slider
0V while the gate output is at 10V and 10V while it is at 0V, changing only at a trigger

notes: Nothing here runs on its own. All three outputs change only when the input jack reaches 1V, and before the first trigger all three read 0V.
Because the outputs start at 0V, the inverted gate output reads 0V until the first trigger rather than the 10V its name implies.
The gate lasts until the next trigger arrives; there is no timer, so the pattern of gates depends entirely on how often the input is clocked.
The module has no menu of its own beyond Rack's.

inputs.0:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
